messages:
Jordan: Escalation from Support — BetaFoods onboarding is blocked. Bulk ingest job failing with repeated OOMs, ~50% failure rate. Customer is asking for an ETA. Ticket #4248. @Marco @Priya can you triage and advise comms?

Marco: On it. Quick clarifying question — is this Hosted or Dedicated?

Jordan: Hosted (eu-west1). Model pinned to gpt-35r-open. Batch job sends ~500 documents in one call. Logs attached below.

Jordan: ```
ERROR: cudnn out of memory at stream 0
Context size: 2048, batch_tokens: 120000
GPU memory used: 93%
Request id: r-8a2f
```

Priya: I'll take ownership of customer comms. Marco — can you draft a short customer-facing cause + mitigation and a temporary workaround we can push right away?

Marco: Short version: workload pattern + large single-request batching is exhausting KV cache and GPU memory. Temporary mitigation: reduce batch_size to <=50 per request and enable prefix/KV caching if not already on. We're also looking at runtime kernel fallback for very large sequences.

Jordan: Repro running with batch_size=50 now. If that passes, we can recommend it as immediate mitigation. Will post perf numbers in ~30m. Setting internal priority to P1.

OnCallBot: Support priority escalated: P1. Notifying eng-support and reducing suppression window.

Emily: I'll prep the customer-facing note. Draft idea: "Thanks — we see the issue is due to very large single requests. Short-term: please try sending smaller batches (<=50 docs) and enable prefix caching; we're testing a runtime patch and will update in 2h." Want to run this by you, Priya. :eyes:

Priya: That sounds right. Add a clear heading: "Immediate action to restore ingestion" and include exact command snippet they can run. Keep a timeline: what we did, immediate workaround, expected next update in 2 hours.

Marco: Command to suggest:```bash
# client-side: split into 50-doc slices
for slice in $(split --lines=50 docs.json); do 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @${slice} 
done
```
Works for Hosted customers. Also include: if they need to keep larger batches, we can schedule a dedicated capacity test.

Jordan: Repro complete: batch_size=50 => no OOM, latency per doc ~120ms, success 100% for the test set. Attaching small perf table.

Priya: Great. Emily can you send the note and propose a 2pm CET customer call to walk them through the workaround? I'll be on the call and provide timeline for patch.

Emily: Sent draft to @BetaFoods primary contact and cc'd AE. Proposed call for 14:00 CET. Included the workaround and the short-term ETA.

Marco: Engineering follow-up: creating a ticket for runtime kernel tweak and automated batch size validation in the serving layer. ETA for engineering patch: EOD + testing tomorrow.

Jordan: Linking internal ticket: INF-1167. Will add logs and perf artifacts.

Priya: Comms plan recap: 1) Immediate: customer runs batch_size=50 workaround (done). 2) Today: eng runs patch testing and provides update by EOD. 3) Tomorrow: deploy candidate to canary; update customer. 4) If needed: propose Dedicated pilot for sustained large-batch ingestion.

Emily: Customer accepted the workaround and confirmed the 14:00 CET call. They sound relieved but flagged potential renewal concern if onboarding delays continue — noted for renewal risk watch. :white_check_mark:

Marco: I'll own the engineering ticket and loop eng-runtime. Priya — if this looks good, close escalation in Support once customer confirms ingestion is stable after the call.

Priya: Good plan. I'll run the call and post a brief summary here after. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
